pred_ddx.label: Tendinosis or tendinitis of the rotator cuff

Rotator cuff tear: The patient's symptoms of pain and weakness in the right shoulder, especially with external rotation and abduction, are consistent with a rotator cuff injury. The physical exam findings of prominent weakness of external rotation and sudden dropping of the arm when lowering it from an overhead position also support this diagnosis. The patient's history of diabetes and obesity may have contributed to the development of a rotator cuff injury.
Tendinosis or tendinitis of the rotator: The patient's symptoms of pain and weakness in the right shoulder, especially with external rotation and abduction, could also be consistent with tendinosis or tendinitis of the rotator cuff. However, the sudden dropping of the arm when lowering it from an overhead position and the significant weakness in shoulder abduction suggest a more severe injury, such as a rotator cuff tear.
